title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། འེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 192)
shelf_note: Derge Tengyur Pramāṇa (ཚད་མ, tshad ma) volume 'e (འེ, vol. 192), containing Buddhist epistemological commentary.

ocr_errors.problem: Negative particle མ་ omitted before ཡིན་པ་, reversing the sense from 'not omniscient' to 'is omniscient'

tr_errors_B.english: Because birth is impossible, it would follow that everything must be examined as being omniscience itself.
tr_errors_B.problem: Misparses ཐམས་ཅད་མཁྱེན་པ་ཉིད་ (omniscience / sarvajñatva) by isolating ཐམས་ཅད་ as 'everything', garbling the opening reductio argument

tr_errors_B.english: Alternatively, whatever are the objects of knowledge for that consciousness, that is the knowledge of that person; being empty of that means being an omniscient being.
tr_errors_B.problem: Reverses the core epistemological thesis by stating that being devoid of the knowledge of knowable objects makes one an omniscient being (asserting the exact opposite of 'not omniscient')

pages.prefer_reason: Translation A accurately renders Pramāṇa terminology and maintains logical coherence, whereas Translation B reverses the core epistemological conclusion by claiming that lacking knowledge makes one omniscient.

book_verdict: Clear woodblock folio from the Derge Tengyur Pramāṇa section; OCR has one serious omission of a negative particle, which misled Translation B into reversing a key logical claim, while Translation A remains precise and faithful.
